metadata.note: The Lehigh and New England's passenger services and their predecessors on the same track: the Pennsylvania, Poughkeepsie and Boston's 1890 opening Slatington - Campbell Hall; the CNJ-operated Lehigh and Lackawanna / Wind Gap and Delaware (Bethlehem - Chapman - Wind Gap - Pen Argyl) to 1904; the L&NE's own trains from 1897 (Slatington - Pen Argyl - Portland - Hainesburg Jct, NYS&W trackage to Swartswood Jct) and from 1905 (Bethlehem - Pen Argyl); its 1927/28-1937 Brill gas-electric cars (Tamaqua - Hauto - Summit Hill; Swartswood - Goshen). The independent Crane Railroad's 1905-06 Catasauqua shuttle (report block [17]) is NOT drawn: neither its track nor either terminal could be located, so any line would be a guess. Only the years the research report marks drawable are drawn. Research report: research/branches/lehigh_and_new_england_railroad.txt.

Panther Creek: CNJ trains and the L&NE car shared the track at the same time - separate operators, not a split; the CNJ trains are not in this layer. Crane Railroad (merged into L&NE 1914) is a separate operator; its 1905-06 shuttle is not drawn (location unknown). LC&N control of the L&NE (1904) and USRA (1918-20) are not splits.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS (last confirmed year, not a known end): Slatington - Pen Argyl 1906 (lne-slatington-pen-argyl-via-wind-gap); Pen Argyl - Portland 1906; Portland - Hainesburg Jct 1902; Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct 1902 [ANCHOR]; PP&B 1890 [ANCHOR]; Bethlehem - Pen Argyl 1929.

THE 1930 CONFLICT: Drury (via american-rails.com p.196) says that by 1930 the L&NE ran only "local trains on ten miles at the Pennsylvania end and a single train in New York"; Kulp says steam Bethlehem - Pen Argyl service ran to 1938, and american-rails.com lists Bethlehem - Pen Argyl as a gas-electric run. lne-bethlehem-pen-argyl is drawn only to 1929 until a 1930s L&NE timetable or Official Guide settles it.
GAS-ELECTRIC DATES: Kulp 1926 / 1928 cars and 1937 end vs american-rails.com 1927-30 cars and 1938 end; inner years drawn.

1891-1896: Reading (28 Apr 1892 - 31 Jul 1893), then Lehigh Valley (Hainesburg Jct - Slatington) and NYS&W (Swartswood Jct - Liberty Corners) to 31 Dec 1896; Fowler's 1893t proves trains but not whose. Nothing drawn.
1897-1927 east of Hainesburg Jct (Swartswood - Sussex - Pine Island - Campbell Hall) undated; the L&NE never drawn to Campbell Hall; when Campbell Hall service ended is unknown.
Whether the NYS&W ran its own passenger trains on Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct.
Pre-1890 CNJ service on Chapman - Wind Gap (1878) and Wind Gap - Pen Argyl - Bangor (1882-83); 1867-1874 on Bethlehem - Chapman.
ICC CNJ Hauto - Tamaqua arrangement "from April 1, 1916" - direction of the lease not established.
Nazareth, Bangor, Saylorsburg, Allentown and Glenwood branches: no confirmable passenger year - omitted (drawable: NONE).
Which of the two parallel Benders - Pen Argyl grades in OSM is the 1897 own line and which the L&L is inferred from mileage and from which one passes Wind Gap borough, not from a source map.
Crane Railroad shuttle (1905-06, report block [17]): route and terminal locations unknown, so it is omitted from the map; draw it only once a map or plan locates it.

properties.line: Pennsylvania, Poughkeepsie and Boston: Slatington – Campbell Hall
properties.speed_source: estimated: single-track steam local and through service over a hilly line; no running times were read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-21), routed with opstrace.py. old_railway_operator probed in (40.5,-76.1,41.6,-74.2): the road is tagged "L&NE" (200 ways; no LNE / Lehigh and New England spelling in that key). The Lehigh and Lackawanna is also tagged "L&NE" (its last owner), not CNJ. OpenHistoricalMap fetched for every lifted stretch; it held nothing on the L&NE/L&L and was not used by the router. The Plainfield Township Recreational Trail near Wind Gap is tagged DL&W (Bangor and Portland) in OSM and was NOT used; the Paulinskill Valley Trail is NYS&W and is used only for the Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct trackage. Pine Island Jct - Campbell Hall routed over Erie-tagged / active track.
properties.geometry_quality: Composite of the traced pieces below, 94.1 mi drawn against about 95 mi documented (Fowler chainage: Slatington 0 - Danielsville 7.0, then Danielsville 42.1 - Pen Argyl 57.8 - Hainesburg Jct 70.1 - Pine Island Jct 113.4, i.e. ~78.3 mi Slatington - Pine Island Jct, plus 16.84 mi of Erie trackage per the ICC; Fowler NY puts Campbell Hall at 130.5). Pieces: Slatington - Benders Jct 14.0 mi (doc 14.4); Benders Jct - Pen Argyl via Wind Gap 8.4 (doc 8.3); Pen Argyl - Portland 9.8 (doc 9.8); Portland - Hainesburg Jct 2.5 (doc 2.5); Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct 18.6 (doc 18.5, NYS&W track); Swartswood Jct - Pine Island Jct 24.8 (doc ~24.8); Pine Island Jct - Goshen 11.1 and Goshen - Campbell Hall 4.8 (Erie track; doc 16.84 together per ICC). STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS: Delaware River crossing Portland - Columbia 0.61 mi (bridge removed, not mapped); Paulinskill Valley Trail gap west of Blairstown 0.47 mi; Erie Montgomery branch north of Goshen, where OSM maps the lifted grade only in fragments, 1.5 mi. Short hand joins of under 0.2 km at Pine Island Jct and Goshen (Erie junction tracks). Benders Jct - Pen Argyl is drawn on the southern of the two parallel grades, through Wind Gap borough (OSM ways 23934055 + 1459543188, L&NE-tagged abandoned grade, hand-assembled because the router kept jumping to the parallel grade; a 185 m (0.1 mi) unmapped gap at Wind Gap is bridged straight): the Lehigh and Lackawanna / Wind Gap and Delaware line. Benders - Wind Gap - Pen Argyl measures 8.4 mi against Fowler's 8.3 (49.5 - 55.6 - 57.8). Identification of which parallel grade is which rests on that mileage fit and on which one passes Wind Gap; no source maps them. TRACKAGE: Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct is New York, Susquehanna and Western track (Paulinskill Valley Trail grade) and Pine Island Jct - Goshen - Campbell Hall is Erie track; the PP&B owned neither. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: every leg is the alignment as it survived into the OSM era; no relocation between 1890 and abandonment is recorded in the report except the Benders - Pen Argyl question above. The Bangor Jct waypoint was placed by estimate; the line passes 0.8 km from it.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] The PP&B opened "ca. Jan. 1, 1890 ... over its entire length with revenue passenger between Campbell Hall, N.Y., and Slatington, Pa." (PRR chronology 1890), and on 30 Jun 1890 Washington - Boston through sleepers ran "via Reading to Bethlehem, CNJ to Pen Argyl, Pennsylvania, Poughkeepsie & Boston to Campbell Hall". 1890 is the only dated PP&B passenger year. The PP&B ran its own trains until the Reading took it over under contract with the receivers on 28 Apr 1892 (PRRC), so service certainly ran wider than 1890, but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor. 1891-1896 are deliberately NOT drawn: Fowler's "1893t" proves passenger trains in 1893 but the timetable's month and issuing company (Reading to 31 Jul 1893, then Lehigh Valley on Hainesburg Jct - Slatington and NYS&W on Swartswood Jct - Liberty Corners until 31 Dec 1896, per the ICC) are unknown, so no operator can be assigned. Route as drawn: Slatington - Benders Jct on PP&B track; Benders Jct - Wind Gap over the Lehigh and Lackawanna (CNJ-operated), as the PP&B did 1890-96; Pen Argyl - Portland on Wind Gap and Delaware metal; Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct over NYS&W track - this leg rests only on the through-route inference (no station-level 1890 evidence; low confidence); Swartswood Jct - Pine Island Jct own track; Pine Island Jct - Goshen - Campbell Hall over the Erie (Pine Island and Montgomery branches). Headway 720 min (about two trains each way) is an estimate; no timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: PRR T&HS chronology 1890 (opening, through sleepers), 1892-93 (Reading contract); ICC valuation (operators to 31 Dec 1896; NYS&W and Erie trackage); report research/branches/lehigh_and_new_england_railroad.txt blocks [1]-[5]. The Hainesburg Jct - Swartswood Jct leg is a route inference only.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 22.4 mi against about 22 mi documented (Slatington 0 - Danielsville 7.0; Danielsville 42.1 - Benders 49.5 - L&L Connection 57.0 - Pen Argyl 57.8). Slatington - Benders Jct 14.0 mi on the L&NE-tagged Slatington branch grade (the southern of the two lines out of Danielsville, through Walnutport; the northern one via Berlinsville is taken to be the 1912 Tamaqua extension (inferred from its course toward Lehigh Gap) and is not drawn; Berlinsville station is therefore ~1 km off the drawn line). Benders Jct - Pen Argyl is drawn on the northern of the two parallel L&NE-tagged grades (OSM way 23931137, via Katellen and Bushkill Township, joining the Wind Gap line at the 'Lehigh & Lackawanna Connection' 0.6 mi west of Pen Argyl): the L&NE's own 1896/97 line. Identification is by mileage and position, not by a source naming the OSM way: this grade measures 7.8 mi Benders - Connection against Fowler's 7.5 mi (49.5 - 57.0), and it does not pass Wind Gap borough. No straight-line legs. Router mileage by operator: L&NE-tagged 100%.

segments.note: The Lehigh and New England operated its own property from 1 Jan 1897 (ICC; Kulp). Positive passenger years on Slatington - Pen Argyl: 1897 (Fowler "Lehigh & Lackawanna Connection 1897G"), 1899 ("Rismillers 1899G" = Horn Springs), 1906 ("Hower's Junction 1906t"). The 13 Aug 1900 Slatington crash (New-York Tribune) involved a special of engine and one car and is not used as evidence of timetabled service. Kulp: passenger service "in more prosperous days had extended from Slatington ... to Campbell Hall" (undated). This feature is the 1897-1904 alignment: the L&NE built its own Benders Jct - Pen Argyl line in 1896/97 (ICC "Pen Argyl to Benders Junction: 1896"; Kulp 1897) and used it until the Lehigh and Lackawanna merger of 14 Oct 1904 / CNJ hand-over in early 1905, after which service was diverted to the L&L line via Wind Gap (Fowler 329) - continues as feature lne-slatington-pen-argyl-via-wind-gap. 1899G confirms service in the middle of the span. Headway is an estimate; no timetable was read for it.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler PA 328-329 (1897G, 1899G); ICC valuation (own operation from 1 Jan 1897; Benders - Pen Argyl built 1896); Kulp (1897 line, later diversion); report research/branches/lehigh_and_new_england_railroad.txt blocks [1], [10].

segments.note: [OPEN] The Lehigh and New England operated its own property from 1 Jan 1897 (ICC; Kulp). Positive passenger years on Slatington - Pen Argyl: 1897 (Fowler "Lehigh & Lackawanna Connection 1897G"), 1899 ("Rismillers 1899G" = Horn Springs), 1906 ("Hower's Junction 1906t"). Drury (via american-rails.com) says that by 1930 the only Pennsylvania passenger service was ten miles at the Tamaqua end, so it had ended by 1930 - the end lies somewhere in 1907-1929, undated. Danielsville - Slatington was abandoned 1928-35 (Kulp); that is not the passenger end. Headway is an estimate; no timetable was read for it.
